title.narrative: OP2.2 Number of public dialogues between CSOs and local government held regarding the promotion of women and youth SMME with the support of the project

description.narrative: This indicator uses the number of dialogues held in the targeted domains to address the diverse and multifaceted interests of different groups in society and for promoting the culture of dialogue. Policy Dialogues refers to the discussions and debate premised on a policy issues and the decisionmaking process associated with that policy. It also implies as a multidimensional, nonlinear and a purposeful exchange or a reflective process that involves people from different interest groups who discuss an issue in which they have a mutual interest. Number of dialogues held on the different policy matter can and will constitute a count either attended or not attended by the same participants.

comment.narrative: The other source of data is the minutes of the meetings.
Disaggregated by the district
3 Indistrict dialogue were conducted with one in each district. 1 National Dialogue held in Maseru consisting of 3 districts.

title.narrative: OP2.4 Number of participants in Participatory Action Research (PAR) conducted with the support of the project.

description.narrative: This indicator uses the number of participants that took part in the conducted research. The Participatory Action Research is strongly value oriented, seeking to address issues of significance concerning the flourishing of human welfare, their communities and the wider ecology in which they participate. With the indicator, it has to be noted therefore that participants are not subject of research, but rather active contributors to research who participate in all phases of the research process. This indicator will be a count of the sample of the participants partaking in the PAR. The process of PAR helps rebuild individuals capacity to be creative actors while being active participants in meaningful policy and decisionmaking processes. The ultimate aim of the PAR is the empowerment of the women and youth led CSOs, local CSO focused enterprises, local authorities, BDS and local authorities to partner and identify priorities, which encourages capacity development and capacity building of all who participate in it.

title.narrative: OP1.4 Focus Group Discussions held to unpack specific legal and gender barriers for enterprise support.

description.narrative: The Focus Group Discussions were held with the objectives of identifying legal and nonlegal challenges the CBOs and youth in the focus areas are faced with in their pursuit of enterprise development. The FDGs were used as a tool to inform and update the beneficiaries on the upcoming capacity building interventions to focus on Gender, Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI). The discussions were around lack of the market and diversification of the enterprises, access to information, capital and business support services.

title.narrative: OP1.1 Training of CSO representatives and their capacities enhanced in understanding of policy decision making processes with the support of the project.

description.narrative: The how government works training were conducted in the Maseru, Leribe and Buthabuthe with the objective to enhance the institutional capacities of the women and youth led CSOs and enterprises on governance processes, the roles of government in promoting entrepreneurship development through its different ministries and parastatals, and the policy decisionmaking spheres within the enterprise ecosystem. The participants understood and appreciated the role of government in promoting employability and economy through the enterprises and how the participants can better be positioned to contribute to the policy formulation processes and the implementation thereof. The participants identified entry points and the legal framework governing their enterprises, opportunities and the interrelation of the well coordinated government ministries, private and parastatals in the promotion of the enterprise growth and development.

title.narrative: OP2.3 local Governance Structures representatives knowledge and capacities enhanced through training on participatory Governance and inclusion in enterprise development and policy decision making processes.

description.narrative: The participatory governance training for the council members comprised of the District Administrators, District Council Secretary (DCS), Chiefs and Councillors in ButhaButhe, Leribe and Maseru in January and February. The training was based and facilitated based on the module development conducted by the expert. The module focused on enhancing the capacities and knowledge of the participants on the following areas: Inclusive policy development, youth inclusion, participation, gender mainstreaming and good governance. The module comprised of the gender components putting emphasis on the importance of gender equity and equality to community development with other key aspects on gender budgeting, gender audits of institutions and gender mainstreaming strategies at the community level. A total of 78 participants were trained in Leribe and ButhaButhe. The other prominent component the participants were trained on are youth in entrepreneurship, youth development support initiatives, youth development targets and local statutes, youth mainstreaming in business and grassroot youth inclusion strategies.
